The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Let $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ be nonempty and open, let $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$, and define
$$Y:=\{(n,s)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R:(1/n,s/n)\in X\},\qquad \varepsilon(n,s):=n\,e(1/n,s/n).$$
For $(n,s)\in Y$, put $v=1/n$, $\sigma_p=s/n$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, $H=e+pv$, $h=\varepsilon+p=nH$, and $\mu=H-T\sigma_p$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Then the following identities hold as equalities of differentials on $Y$:
$$d\varepsilon=T\,ds+\mu\,dn,\qquad \varepsilon+p=Ts+\mu n,\qquad dp=s\,dT+n\,d\mu.$$

For parcel totals $\mathsf S\in\mathbb R$ (entropy), $\mathsf V>0$ (proper volume), and $\mathsf N>0$ (marker count) with $(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N)\in X$, define
$$E(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N):=\mathsf N\,e(\mathsf V/\mathsf N,\mathsf S/\mathsf N).$$
Then $E$ is $C^2$, is positively homogeneous of degree one, and satisfies
$$dE=T\,d\mathsf S-p\,d\mathsf V+\mu\,d\mathsf N,\qquad E=T\mathsf S-p\mathsf V+\mu\mathsf N.$$
If $E$ is viewed on its open domain in $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$, its Hessian annihilates the radial vector $(\mathsf S,\mathsf V,\mathsf N)$.

The local response statements are conditional. At a state with $T>0$ and $e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}>0$, temperature is a valid local coordinate at fixed $v$, and the per-marker heat capacity
$$c_v:=\left(\frac{\partial e}{\partial T}\right)_v=\frac{T}{e_{\sigma_p\sigma_p}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$, the isentropic compressibility
$$\kappa_{\sigma_p}:=-\frac1v\left(\frac{\partial v}{\partial p}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac1{v e_{vv}}$$
is positive. At a state with $e_{vv}>0$ and $h>0$, the local pressure-energy response
$$\alpha_{\sigma_p}:=\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial\varepsilon}\right)_{\sigma_p}=\frac{e_{vv}}{n h}$$
is positive. If $X$ is convex and $e$ is convex on $X$, then $D^2e$ is positive semidefinite. Positivity of the displayed diagonal responses is not asserted to imply convexity, a sound cone, or an evolution theorem.

Let $(M,g,N)$, $u$, $\nabla$, and the fixed-composition state be as in
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]], with
$g(u,u)=-1$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. Define
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $\Delta_{ab}=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$\Delta_a{}^b=\delta_a{}^b+u_au^b$, and $D=u^a\nabla_a$,
$\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and the spatial symmetric
trace-free shear

$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)} -\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$

where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Suppose smooth fields
$\Pi$, $Q^a$, $V^a$, and $\pi^{ab}$ obey $u_aQ^a=u_aV^a=0$,
$u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $\pi^{ab}$ is symmetric with $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Set

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab} +u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a+V^a.$$

If $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$ and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$, the vector field

$$S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T}$$

satisfies the exact identity

$$\nabla_aS^a=-\frac{\Pi\theta+\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T} -\frac{Q^a(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)}{T^2} -V^a\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\mu}{T}\right)-\frac{u_bf^b}{T}.$$

This identity applies to the stated smooth fields and conventions; it does not
select a constitutive law or assert that any such fields solve an evolution
problem.

Let $\mathcal V$ be a four-dimensional real vector space with Lorentz form $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and a chosen future cone. Let $u$ be a future unit timelike vector, $g(u,u)=-1$, and define $\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b$ as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. For every vector $J\in\mathcal V$ and symmetric contravariant rank-two tensor $\mathsf T$ on $\mathcal V$, the following statements hold.

1. The operator $\Delta$ is the $g$-orthogonal projection onto $u^\perp$, and
$$J^a=\nu_u u^a+V^a,\qquad \nu_u=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b,$$
is the unique decomposition with $V\in u^\perp$.

2. With
$$\varepsilon_u=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\quad Q^a=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\quad P^{ab}=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
one has the unique decomposition
$$\mathsf T^{ab}=\varepsilon_u u^a u^b+u^aQ^b+Q^a u^b+P^{ab}.$$
The scalar $p_{\mathrm{mech}}=\tfrac13g_{ab}P^{ab}$ and tensor $\pi^{ab}=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}$ satisfy $u_aQ^a=u_aP^{ab}=0$, $u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Also, $Q=0$ if and only if $u$ is a timelike eigenvector of $\mathsf T^a{}_b$.

3. If $J$ is future timelike, then
$$u_E:=\frac{J}{\sqrt{-g(J,J)}}$$
is the unique future unit timelike frame with vanishing spatial number current; this is the Eckart frame for $J$.

4. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $O\subset M$ be open, and let $\mathsf T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field on $O$. At $x_0\in O$, choose a smooth future tetrad $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ near $x_0$ as supplied by [[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]], and put $u_0:=E_0(x_0)$ and $\Delta_0{}^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u_0^a(u_0)_b$. If
$$\mathsf T^{ab}(x_0)=\varepsilon_0 u_0^a u_0^b+p_0\Delta_0^{ab},\qquad h_0:=\varepsilon_0+p_0>0,$$
then there are a neighborhood $U\subset O$ of $x_0$ and a neighborhood $W$ of $u_0$ in the future unit timelike hyperboloid such that there is a unique $C^1$ future unit timelike field $u_L:U\to W$ with $Q_{u_L}=0$. This field is the local Landau frame. This is a local result; no far-from-equilibrium or global Landau-frame existence is asserted.

5. For every nonzero null $\ell$ and $\rho>0$, the tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}=\rho\ell^a\ell^b$ has no timelike eigenvector and hence no Landau frame.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, let $O\subseteq M$ be open, and let $u$ be a smooth vector field on $O$ satisfying $g(u,u)=-1$ and $g(u,N)<0$ pointwise. Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of $g$. Define
$$
h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_a u_b,\qquad h_a{}^c:=\delta_a{}^c+u_a u^c,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_a u^a,
$$
and the shear
$$
\sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^c h_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac{\theta}{3}h_{ab},
$$
where parentheses denote symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The field $u$ is a future unit timelike observer field in the convention of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Then $\sigma_{ab}$ is symmetric, spatial in both indices ($u^a\sigma_{ab}=u^b\sigma_{ab}=0$), and trace-free ($g^{ab}\sigma_{ab}=0$). The metric restricted to $u^\perp$ is positive definite, so
$$
\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}\ge 0,
$$
with equality exactly when $\sigma_{ab}=0$. More generally, every spatial vector $Y$ satisfies $g_{ab}Y^aY^b\ge0$, with equality exactly when $Y=0$. These are pointwise geometric statements and assume no field equation.

By [F5], the closure $\pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab}$ is symmetric, spatial and trace-free, so it satisfies [F3]'s stress hypotheses; $Q$ is spatial by [F4], and $V=0$. Since $u_bf^b=0$, the remaining balance hypotheses of [F3] also hold. Its entropy current reduces to $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$. Because $Q$ is spatial, $Q^a(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)=Q^aX_a$, and therefore $$\nabla_aS^a=-\frac{\Pi\theta}{T}-\frac{\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T}-\frac{Q^aX_a}{T^2}.$$

From $Q^a=-\kappa X^a/c$, $\Pi=-\zeta_{\rm b}c\theta$, and $\pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab}$, the three terms in step 1.1 become, respectively, $\zeta_{\rm b}c\theta^2/T$, $2\eta c\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}/T$, and $\kappa X^aX_a/(cT^2)$. The vector $X$ is spatial by [F4], so [F5]'s positive-definite rest metric gives $X^aX_a\ge0$; the same fact in [F5] gives $\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}\ge0$. Since $c,T>0$ and the coefficient functions are nonnegative, their sum is the stated identity and is nonnegative.

The scalar $p_{\mathrm{mech}}=\tfrac13g_{ab}P^{ab}$ and tensor $\pi^{ab}=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}$ satisfy $u_aQ^a=u_aP^{ab}=0$, $u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Also, $Q=0$ if and only if $u$ is a timelike eigenvector of $\mathsf T^a{}_b$.

3. If $J$ is future timelike, then
$$u_E:=\frac{J}{\sqrt{-g(J,J)}}$$
is the unique future unit timelike frame with vanishing spatial number current; this is the Eckart frame for $J$.

4. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let $O\subset M$ be open, and let $\mathsf T$ be a $C^1$ symmetric tensor field on $O$. At $x_0\in O$, choose a smooth future tetrad $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ near $x_0$ as supplied by [[thm-gr-local-lorentz-tetrad-existence]], and put $u_0:=E_0(x_0)$ and $\Delta_0{}^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u_0^a(u_0)_b$. If
$$\mathsf T^{ab}(x_0)=\varepsilon_0 u_0^a u_0^b+p_0\Delta_0^{ab},\qquad h_0:=\varepsilon_0+p_0>0,$$
then there are a neighborhood $U\subset O$ of $x_0$ and a neighborhood $W$ of $u_0$ in the future unit timelike hyperboloid such that there is a unique $C^1$ future unit timelike field $u_L:U\to W$ with $Q_{u_L}=0$. 5. For every nonzero null $\ell$ and $\rho>0$, the tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}=\rho\ell^a\ell^b$ has no timelike eigenvector and hence no Landau frame.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Use a smooth time-oriented Lorentz four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], with the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ when assigning physical units: $g$ and the components of $u$ are dimensionless, and $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The physical reading of the geometry is not asserted here.

Let $O\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set and let $u$ be an observer congruence on $O$ in the sense of [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]: $u$ is a smooth vector field whose values are future-directed unit timelike observers, so $g(u,u)=-1$. Its maximal integral curves have open interval parameter domains and are smooth regular future timelike curves; no completeness, geodesic equation, or orthogonal rest-space foliation is assumed. The frame in this definition means this congruence field and its associated pointwise rest spaces. It is not an adapted chart or a tetrad field; those are distinct objects in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]] and [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$
For any vector $X^a$, write $\Delta X$ for $\Delta^a{}_bX^b$. This defines a tensor field; its projection properties are proved in the accompanying fluid-frame lemma.

A local material state consists of a nonempty open set $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$, coordinates $(v,\sigma_p)$ on $X$, and a specified $e\in C^2(X,\mathbb R)$. A **marker** is a formal counted constituent used to normalize these state quantities; calling it conserved does not impose a spacetime conservation equation. Here $v$ is the positive rest-volume-per-marker state coordinate, interpreted as volume measured in the observer's local rest space; the model selects no spatial region whose volume is being integrated. It has units $\mathrm{m^3\,marker^{-1}}$. The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$
Thus $n$ has units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $s$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $\varepsilon,p,h$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{Pa}$, $T$ has units $\mathrm K$, and $H,\mu$ have units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. These are mathematical state maps from the supplied function $e$; no constitutive law is asserted to describe an actual material.

A geometric number current is a $C^1$ vector field $J^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cJ$, with units $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Define its frame density and spatial part by
$$\nu_u:=-u_aJ^a,\qquad V^a:=\Delta^a{}_bJ^b.$$
A geometric entropy current is a $C^1$ vector field $S^a$ with components of units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; its physical flux is $cS$, with units $\mathrm{W\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$. Define
$$s_u:=-u_aS^a,\qquad \Sigma^a:=\Delta^a{}_bS^b.$$
A geometric stress-energy current is a $C^1$ symmetric contravariant tensor field $\mathsf T^{ab}$ with components of units $\mathrm{Pa}$. Define its frame projections
$$\varepsilon_u:=\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b,\qquad Q^a:=-\Delta^a{}_c\mathsf T^{cd}u_d,\qquad P^{ab}:=\Delta^a{}_c\Delta^b{}_d\mathsf T^{cd},$$
$$p_{\mathrm{mech}}:=\tfrac13 g_{ab}P^{ab},\qquad \pi^{ab}:=P^{ab}-p_{\mathrm{mech}}\Delta^{ab}.$$
Here $Q$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$ and $cQ$ is physical energy flux with units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$; $P,p_{\mathrm{mech}},\pi$ have units $\mathrm{Pa}$. The thermodynamic quantities $(\varepsilon,p)$ and the tensor projections $(\varepsilon_u,p_{\mathrm{mech}})$ are not identified by this definition.

For these $C^1$ fields, $\nabla_aJ^a$ and $\nabla_aS^a$ denote scalar covariant divergences, and $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}$ denotes the vector covariant divergence, using the connection fixed above. No conservation equation, perfect-fluid stress form, equality $\nu_u=n$, equality $s_u=s$, or physical interpretation is imposed.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, let $O\subseteq M$ be nonempty and open, and let $u$ be a smooth future unit timelike vector field on $O$. Use the metric-compatible torsion-free connection $\nabla$ and a smooth local state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$ with $X\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ open and $e\in C^\infty(X)$, as in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]. Thus $n=v^{-1}>0$, $s=n\sigma_p$, $\epsilon=ne$, $T=e_{\sigma_p}$, $p=-e_v$, and $\mu=e+pv-T\sigma_p$; assume $T>0$ on $O$ and the Gibbs and Euler identities of [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. Use the convention $x^0=ct$ with $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Define $\Delta^a{}_b=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b$, $\Delta^{ab}=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c$, $\Delta_{ab}=g_{ab}+u_a u_b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, and $a^b=D u^b$. Let $\sigma_{ab}$ be the shear defined in [[lem-tgr-spatial-shear-properties]]: the spatially projected symmetrized derivative of $u$, minus $\theta\Delta_{ab}/3$, with averaged symmetrization. That lemma proves $\sigma$ symmetric, spatial, trace-free, and of nonnegative squared norm. Let $\kappa,\eta,\zeta_{\rm b}\in C^\infty(O)$ be pointwise nonnegative, with SI units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$ and $\mathrm{Pa\,s}$, respectively. Put
$$
X^a=\Delta^{ab}(\nabla_bT+Ta_b),\qquad q^a=-\kappa X^a,\qquad Q^a=q^a/c,
$$
so $q$ is the physical heat flux and $Q$ is its geometric stress component. Set the particle-diffusion current $V^a=0$, the bulk correction $\Pi=-\zeta_{\rm b}c\theta$, and the symmetric spatial trace-free stress $\pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab}$. Suppose $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ for $J^a=nu^a$, and suppose the symmetric stress
$$
\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab}+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab}
$$
satisfies $\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}=f^b$ with zero local power $u_bf^b=0$. Then for $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ the exact entropy-production identity is
$$
\nabla_aS^a=\frac{\kappa}{cT^2}X^aX_a+\frac{2\eta c}{T}\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}+\frac{\zeta_{\rm b}c}{T}\theta^2\ge0.
$$
The conclusion is a conditional identity for the stated smooth fields and closure; it asserts neither existence nor causality, stability, or empirical applicability of an evolution.

Let $(M,g,N_0)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], and let
$\nabla$ be its unique torsion-free $g$-compatible connection supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix a nonempty
connected open set $O\subseteq M$. A **selected stationary thermal carrier** on
$O$ consists of a smooth future timelike vector field $\xi$ and a smooth
positive scalar field $T:O\to(0,\infty)$, where $T$ is measured in kelvins,
such that $\xi$ is a Killing field of $g$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-killing-field]]. Equivalently, the criterion is
$\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$ by
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. The round brackets mean
symmetrization with factor $1/2$. The choice of $\xi$ specifies the thermal congruence; no
coordinate chart or universal observer field is selected.

Set $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and $u:=\xi/N_\xi$. Then
$g(u,u)=-1$. In the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$, $u$ is
dimensionless and $cu$ is the physical four-velocity, with $c>0$ in
$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. For a fixed Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in
$\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, define the inverse-temperature vector
$\beta:=u/(k_BT)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the Killing-normalized
temperature field $T_K:=N_\xi T$. Thus $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$; this definition
does not assert that $T_K$ is constant.

For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, put
$\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$, a dimensionless scalar. Define the rest-space metric,
derivative, acceleration, expansion and shear by
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\qquad D:=u^a\nabla_a,\qquad a_b:=u^a\nabla_au_b,\qquad \theta:=\nabla_au^a,\qquad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)}-\frac13\theta h_{ab}.$$
Here $a$, $\theta$ and $\sigma$ have inverse-length units; the physical
proper acceleration is $c^2a$. The smooth tangent-bundle structure used by
the cited GR suppliers assumes the Axiom of Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]; no stronger choice principle is part of this
definition.

Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$
When this holds, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and the Killing congruence has
$$\xi(N_\xi)=0,\qquad a=\nabla\log N_\xi,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0.$$
If $\xi$ is replaced by $b\xi$ with a constant $b>0$, then
$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

Assume Countable Choice and let $n\ge1$, and let
$u_0:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and uniformly continuous. Define
$u(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Gamma(x-y,t)u_0(y)\,dy$ for $t>0$ and
$u(x,0):=u_0(x)$. Then $u$ is $C^\infty$ on
$\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)$, satisfies $\partial_tu=\Delta_xu$ there, is
bounded with $\|u(\cdot,t)\|_\infty\le\|u_0\|_\infty$, and converges locally
uniformly at the initial time:
$\sup_{x\in K}|u(x,t)-u_0(x)|\to0$ as $t\downarrow0^+$ for every compact
$K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$.

Let $n\ge1$ and $t>0$. The **heat kernel on $\mathbb R^n$** is the function

$$\Gamma(x,t):=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{|x|^2}{4t}\Bigr),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n,$$

where $|x|^2=\langle x,x\rangle$ is the Euclidean square of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and $\exp$ is the real exponential function of
[[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]. For fixed $t>0$ the map
$x\mapsto\Gamma(x,t)$ is a composite of the quadratic form with the exponential
and a scalar multiple, so it is $C^\infty$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] by
[[thm-derivative-of-exponential]] and
[[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]], and it is
strictly positive by [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]]. The
spatial Laplacian entering the heat equation is that of
[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].

The **causal extension** of the heat kernel is $\Gamma(x,t)$ for $t>0$ and
$\Gamma(x,t):=0$ for $t\le0$; the displayed formula is not evaluated at $t=0$
as a function value. The normalisation is fixed by the unit-mass identity
proved for the kernel on this page, and the causal extension is used only as a
locally integrable function or, after embedding, as a distribution.

Assume Countable Choice and let $n\ge1$. For every $t>0$: (i) $\Gamma(\cdot,t)>0$
and $\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Gamma(x,t)\,dx=1$; (ii) parabolic scaling:
$\Gamma(\lambda x,\lambda^2t)=\lambda^{-n}\Gamma(x,t)$ for every $\lambda>0$ and
$x\in\mathbb R^n$; (iii) $\Gamma$ is $C^\infty$ on
$\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)$ and solves the heat equation there,
$\partial_t\Gamma(x,t)=\Delta_x\Gamma(x,t)$; (iv) for every multi-index $\alpha$
there is $C_{n,\alpha}<\infty$ with
$|D^\alpha_x\Gamma(x,t)|\le C_{n,\alpha}t^{-(|\alpha|+n)/2}e^{-|x|^2/(8t)}$ for
all $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $t>0$; in particular $\|\Gamma(\cdot,t)\|_1=1$ and
$(\Gamma(\cdot,t))_{t>0}$ is an $L^1$ approximate identity on $\mathbb R^n$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Fix $n \ge 1$ and let $\lambda_n^*$ be the Lebesgue outer set function on $\mathbb{R}^n$
([[def-lebesgue-outer-measure]]). A set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is
**Lebesgue measurable** when

$$\lambda_n^*(A) \;=\; \lambda_n^*(A \cap E) \;+\; \lambda_n^*(A \setminus E) \qquad \text{for every } A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n .$$

This formula makes sense before any outer-measure theorem is invoked. Under
countable choice, [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-is-an-outer-measure-agreeing-with-volume]]
makes $\lambda_n^*$ an outer measure, and the displayed condition is then exactly
Carathéodory measurability in the sense of [[def-caratheodory-measurable-set]].

The family of Lebesgue measurable sets is written $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$,
and **Lebesgue measure** is the restriction

$$\lambda_n \;:=\; \lambda_n^*\!\restriction_{\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)} .$$

On the real line the subscript is dropped and $\lambda := \lambda_1$.

The quantifier over every test set $A$ is part of the condition, and no
hypothesis on $E$ is imposed before it is tested. That
$\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a sigma-algebra and that $\lambda_n$ is a complete
measure on it are not part of this definition: they are proved, under the Axiom
of Countable Choice, in [[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]], which is
recorded in this item's `justified_by` because it is a statement about the
objects introduced here. Until that theorem the symbols $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
and $\lambda_n$ name a family of sets and a restricted set function, nothing more.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $p$ be a real number with
$0<p<\infty$. Write $\mathcal M(X,\mu)$ for the measurable functions
$f:X\to\mathbb R$. For $f\in\mathcal M(X,\mu)$ define the extended-valued
$p$-functional

$$\|f\|_p:=\begin{cases}\left(\int |f|^p\,d\mu\right)^{1/p},&\displaystyle\int |f|^p\,d\mu<\infty,\\+\infty,&\displaystyle\int |f|^p\,d\mu=+\infty.\end{cases}$$

The finite power uses [[def-real-power]], while the second clause avoids
applying real powers to the extended value $+\infty$. The integral is the
nonnegative Lebesgue integral of [[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]].

The class

$$\mathcal L^p(\mu):=\{f\in\mathcal M(X,\mu): \|f\|_p<\infty\}$$

is the measurable-function space used on this page before passing to
almost-everywhere equivalence classes.

For $1\le p<\infty$, the pointwise operations make $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ a real
vector space by
[[thm-calligraphic-l-p-and-l-infinity-are-vector-spaces-for-p-at-least-one]].

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

- For $0<p<\infty$, define an equivalence relation on $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ by
  $$f\sim g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f-g\in\mathcal N(\mu),$$
  and write $L^p(\mu)$ for the set of classes $[f]$.
- For $p=\infty$, define the same relation on $L^\infty(\mu)$ and again write
  $L^\infty(\mu)$ for the set of classes.

Thus an element of $L^p(\mu)$ is an almost-everywhere equivalence class of
measurable representatives.

When $1\le p\le\infty$, the displayed set quotient agrees with the usual
quotient-vector-space construction of
[[def-quotient-vector-space-and-canonical-projection]].

For $0<p<1$, the same class notation is used; under its stated choice hypothesis, the later item
[[thm-the-l-p-distance-for-zero-less-p-less-one-is-a-complete-translation-invariant-metric]]
supplies the metric structure rather than a normed-space structure.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

1. For $1\le p<\infty$, the rule
   $$\|[f]\|_p:=\|f\|_p\qquad([f]\in L^p(\mu))$$
   is well defined on the quotient classes.
2. For $p=\infty$, the rule
   $$\|[f]\|_\infty:=\|f\|_\infty\qquad([f]\in L^\infty(\mu))$$
   is well defined.
3. In either case, with the quotient vector-space operations of
   [[prop-quotient-vector-space-operations-and-projection]], the resulting pair
   $(L^p(\mu),\|\cdot\|_p)$ is a normed space in the sense of
   [[def-norm-and-normed-space]].

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$

$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

Let $\sigma_{ab}$ be the shear defined in [[lem-tgr-spatial-shear-properties]]: the spatially projected symmetrized derivative of $u$, minus $\theta\Delta_{ab}/3$, with averaged symmetrization. That lemma proves $\sigma$ symmetric, spatial, trace-free, and of nonnegative squared norm. $$
X^a=\Delta^{ab}(\nabla_bT+Ta_b),\qquad q^a=-\kappa X^a,\qquad Q^a=q^a/c,
$$
so $q$ is the physical heat flux and $Q$ is its geometric stress component. Suppose $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ for $J^a=nu^a$, and suppose the symmetric stress
$$

The physical four-velocity associated with $u$ is $U=cu$, with $g(U,U)=-c^2$.

At $x\in O$, the rest space is $u^\perp$ as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Put $u_b=g_{bc}u^c$ and define the mixed rest-space endomorphism
$$\Delta^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+u^a u_b,\qquad \Delta^{ab}:=g^{ac}\Delta^b{}_c.$$

The coordinate $\sigma_p$ is entropy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,marker^{-1}}$, and $e$ is energy per marker, with units $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. For a $C^2$ state map $(v,\sigma_p):O\to X$, define
$$n:=v^{-1},\qquad s:=n\sigma_p,\qquad \varepsilon:=ne,\qquad T:=\partial_{\sigma_p}e,\qquad p:=-\partial_v e,$$
$$H:=e+pv,\qquad h:=\varepsilon+p=nH,\qquad \mu:=H-T\sigma_p.$$

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).


**(e) Smooth timelike curves and their scalar normalization.** Before using
these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$
define

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$

The integral is oriented when $s<s_0$. The function $\tau$ is called
**proper time** for this scaling and $U$ the **four-velocity** of the smooth
curve; its increment times $c$ is the Lorentzian length. The well-definedness
proof below shows $\tau'>0$, that $\tau:I\to\tau(I)$ is a smooth
diffeomorphism, and that $U$ is the velocity of $\gamma\circ\tau^{-1}$.
Thus $g(U,U)=-c^2$ and $U$ is future timelike. This introduces the smooth
case before any physical unit reading; the later worldline definition extends
it to its stated $C^k$, endpoint and piecewise-$C^1$ classes. It asserts no
clock coupling, motion law or physical value of $c$.

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

$$\Gamma(x,t):=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{|x|^2}{4t}\Bigr),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^n,$$

[[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and $\exp$ is the real exponential function of
[[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]. For fixed $t>0$ the map

[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]] by
[[thm-derivative-of-exponential]] and
[[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]], and it is
strictly positive by [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]]. The
spatial Laplacian entering the heat equation is that of
[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].

$\Gamma(x,t):=0$ for $t\le0$; the displayed formula is not evaluated at $t=0$
as a function value. The normalisation is fixed by the unit-mass identity
proved for the kernel on this page, and the causal extension is used only as a
locally integrable function or, after embedding, as a distribution.

$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Fix $n \ge 1$ and let $\lambda_n^*$ be the Lebesgue outer set function on $\mathbb{R}^n$
([[def-lebesgue-outer-measure]]). A set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is
**Lebesgue measurable** when

$$\lambda_n^*(A) \;=\; \lambda_n^*(A \cap E) \;+\; \lambda_n^*(A \setminus E) \qquad \text{for every } A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n .$$

This formula makes sense before any outer-measure theorem is invoked. Under
countable choice, [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-is-an-outer-measure-agreeing-with-volume]]
makes $\lambda_n^*$ an outer measure, and the displayed condition is then exactly
Carathéodory measurability in the sense of [[def-caratheodory-measurable-set]].

The family of Lebesgue measurable sets is written $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$,
and **Lebesgue measure** is the restriction

$$\lambda_n \;:=\; \lambda_n^*\!\restriction_{\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)} .$$

On the real line the subscript is dropped and $\lambda := \lambda_1$.

The quantifier over every test set $A$ is part of the condition, and no
hypothesis on $E$ is imposed before it is tested. That
$\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a sigma-algebra and that $\lambda_n$ is a complete
measure on it are not part of this definition: they are proved, under the Axiom
of Countable Choice, in [[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]], which is
recorded in this item's `justified_by` because it is a statement about the
objects introduced here. Until that theorem the symbols $\mathcal{L}(\mathbb{R}^n)$
and $\lambda_n$ name a family of sets and a restricted set function, nothing more.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $p$ be a real number with
$0<p<\infty$. Write $\mathcal M(X,\mu)$ for the measurable functions
$f:X\to\mathbb R$. For $f\in\mathcal M(X,\mu)$ define the extended-valued
$p$-functional

$$\|f\|_p:=\begin{cases}\left(\int |f|^p\,d\mu\right)^{1/p},&\displaystyle\int |f|^p\,d\mu<\infty,\\+\infty,&\displaystyle\int |f|^p\,d\mu=+\infty.\end{cases}$$

The finite power uses [[def-real-power]], while the second clause avoids
applying real powers to the extended value $+\infty$. The integral is the
nonnegative Lebesgue integral of [[def-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]].

The class

$$\mathcal L^p(\mu):=\{f\in\mathcal M(X,\mu): \|f\|_p<\infty\}$$

is the measurable-function space used on this page before passing to
almost-everywhere equivalence classes.

For $1\le p<\infty$, the pointwise operations make $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ a real
vector space by
[[thm-calligraphic-l-p-and-l-infinity-are-vector-spaces-for-p-at-least-one]].

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

- For $0<p<\infty$, define an equivalence relation on $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ by
  $$f\sim g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f-g\in\mathcal N(\mu),$$
  and write $L^p(\mu)$ for the set of classes $[f]$.
- For $p=\infty$, define the same relation on $L^\infty(\mu)$ and again write
  $L^\infty(\mu)$ for the set of classes.

Thus an element of $L^p(\mu)$ is an almost-everywhere equivalence class of
measurable representatives.

When $1\le p\le\infty$, the displayed set quotient agrees with the usual
quotient-vector-space construction of
[[def-quotient-vector-space-and-canonical-projection]].

For $0<p<1$, the same class notation is used; under its stated choice hypothesis, the later item
[[thm-the-l-p-distance-for-zero-less-p-less-one-is-a-complete-translation-invariant-metric]]
supplies the metric structure rather than a normed-space structure.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

1. For $1\le p<\infty$, the rule
   $$\|[f]\|_p:=\|f\|_p\qquad([f]\in L^p(\mu))$$
   is well defined on the quotient classes.
2. For $p=\infty$, the rule
   $$\|[f]\|_\infty:=\|f\|_\infty\qquad([f]\in L^\infty(\mu))$$
   is well defined.
3. In either case, with the quotient vector-space operations of
   [[prop-quotient-vector-space-operations-and-projection]], the resulting pair
   $(L^p(\mu),\|\cdot\|_p)$ is a normed space in the sense of
   [[def-norm-and-normed-space]].

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\xi$ be a smooth vector field
on $M$ ([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). The **Lie
derivative of the metric along $\xi$**, written $\mathcal L_\xi g$, is the
smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field obtained by the flow definition of
[[def-lie-derivative-of-a-tensor-field]] applied to $g$: for the local flow
$\Phi_t$ of $\xi$,

$$\mathcal L_\xi g:=\frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g .$$

The field $\xi$ is a **Killing field** of $(M,g)$ (an **isometry generator**,
or a **Killing vector**) when

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0 .$$

The equivalent local characterization

$$\mathcal L_\xi g=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\nabla_a\xi_b+\nabla_b\xi_a=0,$$

where $\nabla$ is the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and
$\xi_b:=g_{bc}\xi^c$ is the lowered field, is proved in
[[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]] clause (a); the definition
itself asserts neither direction. Whether a given metric has Killing fields is
a property of that metric: neither existence nor uniqueness of a Killing field
is asserted here, and a general metric has none beyond the trivial field
$\xi=0$.

Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ with $L_i>0$, and let $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ be an open neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$. Let $N\in C^\infty(U,(0,\infty))$ satisfy $0<N_{\min}\le N(x)\le N_{\max}<\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$. On $M=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times U$, use $x^0=ct_K$ with $c>0$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, give $M$ the time orientation $\xi=\partial_{x^0}$, and use the metric
$$
g=-N(x)^2(dx^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(dx^i)^2,
$$
where $x^i$ are measured in metres, $t_K$ in seconds, and $N$ is dimensionless. By [[def-gr-killing-field]], a Killing field is one satisfying $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, where $\mathcal L_\xi g=\frac d{dt}|_{t=0}\Phi_t^*g$ for the local flow $\Phi_t$ of $\xi$. Thus $\xi$ is a future timelike Killing field, $N=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}$, and $u=N^{-1}\xi$ is the smooth future unit timelike observer congruence of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]; here this congruence means the unit timelike vector field, not a coordinate chart. Write $\nabla_x$, $\operatorname{div}_x$, $\nu$, and $dx$ for the Euclidean spatial gradient, divergence, outward unit normal, and three-dimensional Lebesgue volume on the box, and set $|\Omega|:=\int_\Omega1\,dx=L_1L_2L_3$. For scalar fields on $\Omega$, $L^2(\Omega)$ and its norm use this measure.

For $t_K>0$ use the open domain $O=(0,\infty)\times\Omega$. Spatial vectors such as $q$ are extended to spacetime with zero $x^0$ component.

Fix constants $C_V,n_0,A_0,T_{\rm ref}>0$, a reference entropy $\sigma_{\rm ref}\in\mathbb R$, and a reference energy $e_0\in\mathbb R$. Their units are $C_V$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}K^{-1}}$, $n_0$ in $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$, $A_0$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $T_{\rm ref}$ in kelvins, $\sigma_{\rm ref}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and $e_0$ in $\mathrm{J\,marker^{-1}}$. Define the derived per-marker heat capacity $c_v=C_V/n_0$, with units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}marker^{-1}}$, and the local mathematical material state function on $X=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ by
$$
e(v,\sigma_p)=c_vT_{\rm ref}\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma_p-\sigma_{\rm ref}}{c_v}\right)+e_0,
$$
independent of $v$. For a positive proper temperature $T$, set $\sigma_p=\sigma_{\rm ref}+c_v\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$ and $v=1/n_0$. The state definitions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] give $n=n_0$, $p=0$, $\epsilon=C_VT+n_0e_0$, and $s=n_0\sigma_{\rm ref}+C_V\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$.

Let $\vartheta_0\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ satisfy $0<m_0\le\vartheta_0\le M_0$ and admit a $C^2$ extension $\widetilde\vartheta_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ with the same bounds, period $2L_i$ in coordinate $x^i$, and evenness under $x^i\mapsto-x^i$ for each $i$. These conditions make the extension even about every face $x^i=0,L_i$. Set $T_0=\vartheta_0/N$. Define the physical heat flux, conductivity, static heat balance, and insulated-face condition by
$$
q=-\kappa_{\rm th}(\nabla_xT+T\nabla_x\log N),\qquad \kappa_{\rm th}=A_0/N,\qquad NC_V\partial_{t_K}T+\operatorname{div}_x(N^2q)=0,\qquad N^2q\cdot\nu=0\ \text{on each face},
$$
where $q$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, $\kappa_{\rm th}$ has units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal to a face. In the entropy identity use zero particle diffusion and zero shear and bulk viscosity, $V=0$ and $\eta=\zeta_{\rm b}=0$, so $\Pi=0$ and $\pi^{ab}=0$. The thermal diffusivity $A_0/C_V$ has units $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$. There is a unique solution $T\in C([0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)\cap C^{2,1}((0,\infty)\times\overline\Omega)$, where $C^{2,1}$ means two continuous spatial derivatives and one continuous time derivative up to the box faces, satisfying the heat balance, the face condition, and the initial condition $T(0,x)=T_0(x)=\vartheta_0(x)/N(x)$. It is given by
$$\vartheta(t_K,x):=N(x)T(t_K,x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma\!\left(x-y,\frac{A_0}{C_V}t_K\right)\widetilde\vartheta_0(y)\,dy\quad(t_K>0),\qquad \vartheta(0,x)=\vartheta_0(x),\qquad \Gamma(z,t)=(4\pi t)^{-3/2}e^{-|z|^2/(4t)},\quad z\in\mathbb R^3,\ t>0.$$
Thus $T=\vartheta/N$. It satisfies $C_V\partial_{t_K}\vartheta=A_0\Delta_x\vartheta$, $\partial_\nu\vartheta=0$ on each face, and $m_0\le\vartheta\le M_0$.

For this solution set $Q^0=0$, $Q^i=q^i/c$, $J=n_0u$, and
$$
\mathsf T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+u^aQ^b+Q^au^b,\qquad f^b:=\nabla_a\mathsf T^{ab}.
$$
Here $Q=q/c$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, $\mathsf T$ has units $\mathrm{Pa}$, and $f$ has units $\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. Then $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ and $u_bf^b=0$: $f$ is an explicitly defined external support that supplies no local power. The entropy current $S^a=su^a+Q^a/T$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}m^{-3}}$ and total entropy $\mathcal S(t_K)=\int_\Omega s(t_K,x)\,dx$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, with
$$
\frac{d\mathcal S}{dt_K}=A_0\int_\Omega\frac{|\nabla_x\vartheta|^2}{\vartheta^2}\,dx\ge0.
$$
The lapse-weighted energy $\mathcal E_K(t_K)=\int_\Omega N\epsilon\,dx$ is constant in $\mathrm{J}$. If $\overline\vartheta=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega\vartheta_0\,dx$ and $C_\Omega=\frac32(\max_iL_i)^2$, then
$$
\left\|\vartheta(t_K,\cdot)-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le \exp\!\left(-\frac{A_0t_K}{C_VC_\Omega}\right)\left\|\vartheta_0-\overline\vartheta\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.
$$
Thus $T$ converges in $L^2(\Omega)$ to $T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta/N$. Since $N T_{\rm eq}=\overline\vartheta>0$, the inverse-temperature vector $\beta=u/(k_BT_{\rm eq})$, for $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, is Killing by [[lem-tgr-killing-thermal-normalization]]. This is a mathematical solution of the specified fixed-background, supported first-order heat model; it asserts no Einstein equation, general dissipative-fluid initial-value theorem, or finite propagation speed.

derivations.claim: Put $r=A_0\pi^2/(C_VL_1^2)>0$. The formula $\widetilde\vartheta_0(x)=\overline\vartheta+\delta\cos(\pi x^1/L_1)$ on $\mathbb R^3$ is smooth, even in each coordinate, and $2L_i$-periodic in each coordinate; $|\delta|<\overline\vartheta$ makes it positive. Its average on $\Omega$ is $\overline\vartheta$, since $$\int_0^{L_1}\cos(\pi x^1/L_1)\,dx^1=\left[\frac{L_1}{\pi}\sin(\pi x^1/L_1)\right]_{0}^{L_1}=0.$$ Differentiating the displayed time-dependent profile gives $\partial_{t_K}\vartheta=-r\delta e^{-rt_K}\cos(\pi x^1/L_1)$ and $\Delta_x\vartheta=-(\pi^2/L_1^2)\delta e^{-rt_K}\cos(\pi x^1/L_1)$. Thus $C_V\partial_{t_K}\vartheta=A_0\Delta_x\vartheta$, and its initial trace is exactly $\vartheta_0$.

The bound $|\delta e^{-rt_K}\cos(\pi x^1/L_1)|\le|\delta|<\overline\vartheta$ proves positivity. Direct differentiation gives $\partial_{x^1}\vartheta=-(\pi\delta/L_1)e^{-rt_K}\sin(\pi x^1/L_1)$, which vanishes at $x^1=0,L_1$; the other two normal derivatives vanish because the profile is independent of $x^2,x^3$. Hence it satisfies every boundary condition of [F1], and uniqueness identifies it with the theorem's heat solution. Using $\cos^2 z=(1+\cos(2z))/2$ and integrating the cosine term over $[0,L_1]$ gives $\int_0^{L_1}\cos^2(\pi x^1/L_1)\,dx^1=L_1/2$. Therefore $$\|\vartheta(t_K,\cdot)-\overline\vartheta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}=|\delta|\sqrt{|\Omega|/2}\,e^{-rt_K}.$$ Dividing by the fixed positive lapse gives $T=\vartheta/N$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary, so that $M$ is Hausdorff
and second countable and carries a maximal smooth atlas
([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $g$ be a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$
in the sense of [[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]. Then $g$ assigns
to every $p\in M$ a bilinear form $g_p:T_pM\times T_pM\to\mathbb R$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]]).

**(a) Lorentzian metric.** The field $g$ is a **Lorentzian metric of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$** on $M$ when it is symmetric and nondegenerate, and at every
$p\in M$ the pair $(T_pM,g_p)$ is a Lorentz vector space of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ in the sense of [[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]: that is, $g_p$ has
inertia $(3,1,0)$, so that some — equivalently every — basis of $T_pM$ in which
the matrix of $g_p$ is diagonal has exactly one negative and three positive
diagonal entries. The pair $(M,g)$ is a **smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** (or
Lorentzian manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$). In a smooth chart $(U,x)$ the
**components** of $g$ are the $C^\infty$ functions
$g_{ab}(q)=g_q(\partial_a|_q,\partial_b|_q)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]], and $g_{ab}=g_{ba}$ by symmetry.
We use indices $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$ and the Einstein summation convention, with
components in a chart written as lower-case indexed symbols and equations
between indexed fields understood basis-independently. These conventions are
fixed once for this library and the physical reading of the symbols is recorded
with the framework postulates, separately from this mathematical definition.

**(b) Pointwise causal structure.** For every $p\in M$ the vocabulary of
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] applies to the Lorentz vector
space $(T_pM,g_p)$: a tangent vector $v\in T_pM$ is **timelike** when
$g_p(v,v)<0$, **null** when $v\neq0$ and $g_p(v,v)=0$, **spacelike** when
$g_p(v,v)>0$, and **causal** when it is timelike or null. Every nonzero
$v\in T_pM$ has exactly one causal character. The **timelike set**
$T_p:=\{v\in T_pM:g_p(v,v)<0\}$ has exactly two connected components, each
nonempty, open, convex and path-connected; each $g_p$-orthonormal basis
$e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $T_pM$ satisfies $g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
for some ordering, so in particular nonzero orthonormal vectors exist at every
point ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]],
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]).

**(c) Time orientation.** A **time orientation** of $(M,g)$, also called a
**choice of future cone**, is a smooth vector field $N$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]], whose tangent-bundle
smooth structure uses the axiom $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of
[[def-countable-choice]]; this is the only use of that axiom in this
definition) such that

$$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0\qquad\text{for every }p\in M .$$

The function $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N_p)$ is $C^\infty$ because $g$ is a smooth
covariant $2$-tensor field and $N$ a smooth field, so the condition is a
pointwise strict inequality between a smooth function and $0$; since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)<0$ implies $N_p\neq0$, a time orientation is nowhere vanishing.
A **time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold** is a triple $(M,g,N)$
consisting of a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and a time orientation $N$.

Given a time orientation $N$ and $p\in M$, the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and we
**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future causal vectors form
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).

these quantities in the physical conventions, fix a positive real scaling
parameter $c$ (with no physical meaning or dimension in this mathematical
item). A **smooth future timelike curve** is a smooth map $\gamma:I\to M$
from a nonempty open real interval $I$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]) whose velocity derivation
$\gamma'(s)\in T_{\gamma(s)}M$
([[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]]) satisfies
$g(\gamma',\gamma')<0$ and $g(\gamma',N)<0$ at every $s\in I$.
In a chart its components are $d(x^a\circ\gamma)/ds$, $a=0,1,2,3$.
For a supplied base point $s_0\in I$ and additive constant $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$

$$h(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s))},\qquad \tau(s):=\tau_0+\frac1c\int_{s_0}^{s}h(r)\,dr,\qquad U(s):=\frac{c\gamma'(s)}{h(s)}.$$
